valid_anagram.brute:
sorted_s = the letters of s, sorted
sorted_t = the letters of t, sorted
if sorted_s == sorted_t: return true   (anagrams sort to the identical sequence)
return false
valid_anagram.optimal:
if length of s != length of t: return false
count = 26 zeros
for each index i:
    letter_s = position of s[i] in the alphabet, letter_t = position of t[i]
    count[letter_s] += 1   (s pushes its column up)
    count[letter_t] -= 1   (t pulls it back down)
for each c in count:
    if c != 0: return false
return true

string_to_integer_atoi.brute:
strip the leading spaces from s
sign = 1
if s starts with "-": sign = -1, drop that character
else if s starts with "+": drop that character
digits = ""
for each ch in s:
    if ch is not a digit: break   (the first non-digit ends the number)
    append ch to digits
if digits is empty: return 0
value = sign * integer value of digits
return value clamped to [INT_MIN, INT_MAX]
string_to_integer_atoi.optimal:
i = 0
while i < n and s[i] == " ": i += 1   (skip leading spaces)
sign = 1
if i < n and s[i] is "+" or "-":
    if s[i] == "-": sign = -1
    i += 1
num = 0
while i < n and s[i] is a digit:
    digit = value of s[i]
    num = num * 10 + digit
    if sign * num >= INT_MAX: return INT_MAX   (clamp as soon as the bound is crossed)
    if sign * num <= INT_MIN: return INT_MIN
    i += 1
return sign * num

minimum_remove_to_make_valid_parentheses.brute:
drop_unmatched(s, opener, closer):
    changed = true
    while changed:
        changed = false, depth = 0
        for each index i in s:
            if s[i] == opener: depth += 1
            else if s[i] == closer: depth -= 1
            if depth < 0:   (this closer has no partner: delete it and restart)
                delete s[i], changed = true, break
    return s
s = drop_unmatched(s, "(", ")")
reversed_s = reverse of s   (read backwards, ")" opens and "(" closes)
reversed_s = drop_unmatched(reversed_s, ")", "(")
return reverse of reversed_s

moving_average_from_data_stream.brute:
init(size):
    size = size, seen = empty list
next(val):
    append val to seen
    tail = the last size values of seen (fewer while the stream is short)
    total = 0
    for each x in tail: total += x   (re-summed from scratch every time)
    return total / size of tail
moving_average_from_data_stream.optimal:
init(size):
    size = size
    window = empty deque, total = 0
next(val):
    push val to the back of window, total += val
    if size of window > size:
        oldest = pop the front   (the value that just slid out of the window)
        total -= oldest
    return total / size of window

logger_rate_limiter.brute:
init:
    printed = empty list of (timestamp, message)
should_print_message(timestamp, message):
    for each (old_time, old_message) in printed:
        if old_message == message and timestamp - old_time < 10: return false
    append (timestamp, message) to printed
    return true
logger_rate_limiter.optimal:
init:
    next_ok = empty dict message -> earliest timestamp it may print again
should_print_message(timestamp, message):
    allowed_at = next_ok[message], or 0 if never seen
    if timestamp < allowed_at: return false
    next_ok[message] = timestamp + 10   (blocked for the next 10 seconds)
    return true

design_hashmap.optimal:
init:
    size = 0, buckets = 8 empty lists
bucket_for(key):
    return buckets[key mod number of buckets]   (keys are ints, so the key is its own hash)
put(key, value):
    bucket = bucket_for(key)
    for each pair in bucket:
        if pair.key == key: pair.value = value, return
    append [key, value] to bucket, size += 1
    if size > 2 * number of buckets: resize   (load factor above 2: double and rehash)
get(key):
    for each pair in bucket_for(key): if pair.key == key, return pair.value
    return -1
remove(key):
    bucket = bucket_for(key)
    for each index i in bucket:
        if bucket[i].key == key: remove bucket[i], size -= 1, return
resize:
    old_buckets = buckets, buckets = twice as many empty lists
    for each pair in every old bucket: append pair to bucket_for(pair.key)

insert_delete_getrandom_o1.brute:
init:
    vals = empty list
insert(val):
    if val is in vals (linear scan): return false
    append val to vals
    return true
remove(val):
    if val is not in vals: return false
    remove val from vals   (scan, then everything after it shifts left)
    return true
get_random:
    return a uniformly random element of vals
insert_delete_getrandom_o1.optimal:
init:
    vals = empty list, index_of = empty dict val -> position in vals
insert(val):
    if val in index_of: return false
    index_of[val] = size of vals   (it will sit at the end of the list)
    append val to vals
    return true
remove(val):
    if val not in index_of: return false
    i = index_of[val], last = last element of vals
    vals[i] = last, index_of[last] = i   (move the last element into the hole)
    pop the last element of vals
    delete val from index_of
    return true
get_random:
    return a uniformly random element of vals

time_based_key_value_store.brute:
init:
    store = empty dict key -> list of (timestamp, value)
set(key, value, timestamp):
    if key not in store: store[key] = empty list
    append (timestamp, value) to store[key]
get(key, timestamp):
    best_time = -1, best_value = ""
    for each (time, value) in store[key]:
        if time <= timestamp and time > best_time:   (newest version not after timestamp)
            best_time = time, best_value = value
    return best_value
time_based_key_value_store.optimal:
init:
    times = empty dict key -> ascending list of timestamps
    values = empty dict key -> values aligned with times
set(key, value, timestamp):
    if key not in times: times[key] = empty list, values[key] = empty list
    append timestamp to times[key]   (strictly increasing, so the list stays sorted)
    append value to values[key]
get(key, timestamp):
    if key not in times: return ""
    lo = 0, hi = size of times[key]
    while lo < hi:   (binary search for the first index whose time is > timestamp)
        mid = (lo + hi) // 2
        if times[key][mid] <= timestamp: lo = mid + 1
        else: hi = mid
    if lo == 0: return ""   (every version is newer than timestamp)
    return values[key][lo - 1]

lru_cache.brute:
init(capacity):
    capacity = capacity
    items = empty list of [key, value], most recently used first
get(key):
    for each index i in items:
        if items[i].key == key:
            move items[i] to the front   (it is now the most recent)
            return its value
    return -1
put(key, value):
    for each index i in items:
        if items[i].key == key: remove items[i], stop scanning
    insert [key, value] at the front
    if size of items > capacity: remove the last item   (the least recently used)
lru_cache.optimal:
init(capacity):
    capacity = capacity, nodes = empty dict key -> node
    head, tail = sentinel nodes linked head <-> tail   (head.next = most recent, tail.prev = least)
unlink(node): node.prev.next = node.next, node.next.prev = node.prev
push_front(node): link node in between head and head.next
get(key):
    if key not in nodes: return -1
    node = nodes[key]
    unlink(node), push_front(node)   (touching a key makes it the most recent)
    return node.val
put(key, value):
    if key in nodes:
        node = nodes[key], node.val = value
        unlink(node)
    else:
        node = new node(key, value), nodes[key] = node
        if size of nodes > capacity:
            victim = tail.prev   (least recently used)
            unlink(victim), delete victim.key from nodes
    push_front(node)
